body: KPV is a synthetic tripeptide built from three amino acids: lysine, proline and valine. The same Lys-Pro-Val sequence forms the C-terminal end of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH), which is why the literature also calls it α-MSH (11–13). Interest in the fragment grew out of 1980s work on α-MSH, when researchers asked how much of the hormone's activity a short tail could carry. Since then, KPV has been studied mainly in cell culture and rodent models of inflammatory signaling, including intestinal models involving the PepT1 peptide transporter.
Veracue presents KPV strictly as a Research Use Only material. It is not for human or veterinary use.

sections.heading: What Is KPV Peptide?
body: KPV peptide is the tripeptide Lys-Pro-Val, corresponding to residues 11 to 13 of α-MSH. In its reference form (CAS 67727-97-3, PubChem CID 125672) it is a free acid with the formula C₁₆H₃₀N₄O₄ and an average molecular weight of about 342.44 g/mol. Published reviews describe KPV as retaining anti-inflammatory activity reported for α-MSH in experimental systems, without the parent hormone's pigmentary action.

Two separate questions sit behind any KPV listing, though. The first concerns the molecule: its sequence, formula and research history. The second concerns a specific vial: whether that material is KPV, in which chemical form, and at what documented purity. Only lot-specific analytical data can answer the second question.

subsections.heading: Molecular Identity and Structure
body: KPV is short enough that every residue matters. Lysine contributes two basic amino groups. Proline adds a ring that restricts backbone flexibility, and valine closes the chain with a small hydrophobic side group. None of the three residues is aromatic, a detail that shapes how KPV behaves in HPLC analysis.

Inside native α-MSH, this sequence sits at an amidated C-terminus. The standalone reference compound indexed in PubChem, however, is the free acid. Because published studies do not always use the same form, terminal chemistry is worth checking before comparing results.

subsections.heading: Mechanistic Research Context
body: The most cited mechanistic work comes from intestinal research. Dalmasso and colleagues (2008) reported that KPV is taken up through PepT1, a di- and tripeptide transporter, in human intestinal epithelial and T-cell lines. In those cells, KPV reduced cytokine-stimulated NF-κB reporter activity and pro-inflammatory signaling.

Other groups reached different conclusions about mechanism. Kannengiesser and colleagues (2008) reported that effects in two mouse colitis models appeared at least partly independent of the MC1R melanocortin receptor. Earlier, Getting and colleagues (2003) found that KPV reduced neutrophil accumulation in a mouse peritonitis model, yet did not suppress macrophage mediator release in vitro. They proposed interference with IL-1β signaling rather than melanocortin-receptor activation.

subsections.heading: Why KPV Appears in Experimental Research
body: KPV lets researchers study one part of α-MSH biology in isolation. Brzoska and colleagues (2008) described it as retaining anti-inflammatory activity while lacking the full hormone's pigmentary action. Its uptake through PepT1 also connects it to peptide-transport research. Later studies, including Laroui and colleagues (2010) and Xiao and colleagues (2017), tested nanoparticle carriers designed to deliver KPV to the colon in mouse colitis models.

subsections.heading: What the Literature Does and Does Not Establish
body: The KPV studies cited here are cell-culture and animal experiments. They show that KPV changed specific measured markers, under specific conditions, in specific models. They do not establish human efficacy, human safety or a human dose. No peer-reviewed human efficacy trial of KPV was identified in the literature reviewed for this page. Mechanism also remains open, since the transporter, receptor and IL-1β hypotheses come from different models and have not been reconciled.

sections.heading: Analytical Characterization of KPV
body: Two methods do most of the work, and each answers a different question.

Reversed-phase HPLC (RP-HPLC) separates the components of a sample. It reports purity as a percentage of total peak area at a stated detection wavelength. For KPV, detection relies on peptide-bond absorbance in the low-UV range, because the molecule has no aromatic side chains. HPLC shows how much of the detected material elutes as the main peak. By itself, it cannot prove that the main peak is KPV.

Mass spectrometry (ESI-MS or LC-MS) measures molecular mass. A result matching the expected mass supports identity, provided the report says whether it shows the neutral mass or a protonated ion. For the free acid, the protonated ion [M+H]⁺ is expected near m/z 343.23. Mass alone, however, cannot tell KPV apart from sequence isomers such as Lys-Val-Pro, or from D-residue variants. Both share its exact formula.

Orthogonal checks close those gaps. Tandem MS (MS/MS) fragmentation supports residue order. Co-elution with a characterized reference standard supports retention identity, and chiral analysis addresses stereochemistry. Not every COA will include all of these. Knowing which questions a document leaves open is part of reading it well.

body: A certificate of analysis describes one manufacturing lot. It is not a general statement about KPV, and it should not be carried over to a different lot. For a molecule this small, and with this many look-alikes, the details on the certificate matter more than the headline purity figure.

sections.heading: KPV Peptide Benefits: What Research Actually Shows
body: Searches for KPV peptide benefits usually ask what the peptide has been shown to do. The accurate answer is narrower than most results suggest, because KPV research describes measured activities in models, not benefits in people.

In human intestinal epithelial and T-cell lines, KPV reduced NF-κB-linked inflammatory signaling after cytokine stimulation (Dalmasso et al., 2008). In mouse colitis models, induced chemically or by T-cell transfer, KPV-treated groups showed lower inflammatory and histological scores than controls (Dalmasso et al., 2008; Kannengiesser et al., 2008). In a mouse ear-swelling model, α-MSH (11–13) inhibited experimentally induced swelling (Hiltz and Lipton, 1989). In a mouse peritonitis model, it reduced neutrophil accumulation (Getting et al., 2003).

Each of these is a finding about a defined experimental system. Together, they do not show reduced inflammation in humans, improved gut or skin health, or any treatment effect. The same literature also contains results where KPV did not act, which is why model choice matters as much as the headline result.

sections.heading: What Does KPV Do?
body: In published experiments, KPV has been observed to enter certain cells through the PepT1 transporter and to dampen NF-κB-linked signaling in stimulated cell lines. In rodent models, it has changed measured inflammatory endpoints. How it does this is still debated. Transporter-dependent, IL-1β-related and melanocortin-receptor-independent explanations all appear in the literature. These are observations about experimental systems. They do not describe what KPV does in a person.

sections.heading: What Is KPV Used For in Research?
body: Researchers study KPV in a handful of connected areas: inflammatory signaling in epithelial and immune cell lines; di- and tripeptide transport through PepT1; structure–function questions about which parts of α-MSH carry which activities; pharmacology in rodent colitis models; and delivery-system design, such as nanoparticle and hydrogel carriers. Analog work, including stereoisomers and the related tripeptide KdPT, adds structure–activity comparisons. None of this constitutes a use for KPV outside the laboratory.

sections.heading: KPV Dosage: Why This Page Gives No Numbers
body: Veracue does not provide KPV dosage, dosing schedules or administration guidance of any kind. Human dosing sits outside the scope of a Research Use Only product page, and no human dose for KPV has been established in peer-reviewed clinical research.

For laboratory work, experimental conditions come from the study design, not from a supplier. They depend on the model, the assay, the chemical form used and the endpoints being measured. Researchers typically start from the primary literature, validate their own assay variables and confirm the identity and net content of the specific lot. Without that last step, results are difficult to compare with published work.

sections.heading: Oral KPV
body: Questions about oral KPV for human use are outside the scope of this page, and Veracue provides no oral-use or formulation guidance. Some published rodent studies tested gut-targeted carrier systems, such as polymer nanoparticles in polysaccharide hydrogels. Those were experimental delivery systems built for animal models. Their results say nothing about how an unformulated research material would behave, and they are not instructions. Formulation questions belong inside a validated research design.

sections.heading: Research Use Only and Regulatory Context
body: KPV is not an FDA-approved drug. In July 2026, KPV free base and KPV acetate were among the bulk substances discussed by the FDA's Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee, in connection with the Section 503A bulk drug substances list. That process concerns pharmacy compounding, not research supply. An advisory discussion is also not an approval.

This material is supplied for laboratory research, scientific investigation and analytical characterization only. It is not intended for human or veterinary use, ingestion, injection or any form of administration, and it has not been evaluated by the FDA for safety or efficacy.

J_problem_research_solutions.heading: Common KPV Research Problems and How to Approach Them

sections.heading: The Name Is Not the Identity
sections.problem: “KPV” appears on single-peptide listings, inside multi-peptide blend names such as KLOW, and as a frequent misspelling (“KVP”). Similar abbreviations, such as KPT and KdPT, describe different peptides.
sections.research_approach: Treat the name as a label. Confirm the full sequence, Lys-Pro-Val, on the lot's documentation. Check whether the material is a single compound or a blend, and in which chemical form it was supplied. For any blend, identity and quantity need documenting for each component separately.

sections.heading: Sequence Isomers Share KPV's Exact Mass
sections.problem: Lys-Val-Pro and Pro-Val-Lys contain the same three residues as KPV and share its formula, C₁₆H₃₀N₄O₄. An intact-mass result cannot tell them apart.
sections.research_approach: Look for evidence of residue order. MS/MS fragmentation breaks the peptide at predictable bonds and reveals sequence. Co-elution with a characterized KPV reference standard offers a second, independent line of support.

sections.heading: Stereochemistry Is Invisible to Mass
sections.problem: The KPV literature includes analogs with D-amino acids, such as KdPV and dKPdV, and early work examined how stereochemistry changed activity. Swapping an L-residue for a D-residue does not change mass.
sections.research_approach: If configuration matters to the study, ask whether it was tested or simply assumed from the synthesis inputs. Chiral analysis, for example after hydrolysis and chiral derivatization, addresses it directly. Standard RP-HPLC and MS may not.

sections.heading: Free Acid, Amide or Acetylated?
sections.problem: Native α-MSH ends in an amidated valine, while the PubChem reference compound is the free acid. Early patent literature described an acetylated, amidated form. Papers do not always use the same one.
sections.research_approach: Match the form to the study being compared. The monoisotopic masses separate them: 342.23 Da for the free acid, 341.24 Da for the amide and 383.25 Da for Ac-KPV-NH₂. A COA should state the form explicitly rather than leave it to inference.

sections.heading: Salt Form and Net Peptide Content
sections.problem: FDA's July 2026 advisory agenda listed KPV free base and KPV acetate as separate substances. Purified peptides are commonly isolated as salts, and KPV's two amine groups can each carry a counter-ion.
sections.research_approach: Weighed powder includes counter-ion and residual water as well as peptide. Look for a named counter-ion and, ideally, a net peptide content figure. Without them, comparisons between lots, or with published work, rest on an unstated assumption.

sections.heading: Purity and Identity Are Different Measurements
sections.problem: A high HPLC percentage is often read as proof that a vial contains KPV. A sample can be chromatographically clean and still be the wrong molecule.
sections.research_approach: Require both measurements. HPLC describes how much of the detected material is the main component. Mass spectrometry describes whether that component has the expected mass. Neither replaces the other.

sections.heading: Reading a KPV HPLC Result
sections.problem: Purity is reported as area percent at one wavelength. KPV has no aromatic residues, so detection depends on low-UV peptide-bond absorbance, where some impurities respond differently. Small, polar peptides can also retain weakly on reversed-phase columns.
sections.research_approach: Ask for the chromatogram, not only the number. Check the detection wavelength, where the main peak elutes relative to the solvent front, and whether minor peaks are integrated. A clean, well-retained peak says more than a percentage alone.

sections.heading: Near-Mass Neighbors and Reporting Conventions
sections.problem: GHK (340.38 g/mol) and KdPT (344.41 g/mol) sit within a few daltons of KPV (342.44 g/mol). Some listings round KPV to “about 340 Da.” The amide's protonated ion (m/z 342.25) also lands almost exactly on the free acid's neutral mass (342.23).
sections.research_approach: Compare observed and theoretical values using the same convention. Check whether the report gives neutral or [M+H]⁺ mass, and whether it uses average or monoisotopic values. The stated tolerance should be tight enough to separate the forms in question.

sections.heading: Keeping KPV Separate from α-MSH
sections.problem: Properties of α-MSH and synthetic melanocortin analogs, such as pigmentation and melanocortin-receptor agonism, are often attributed to KPV by association.
sections.research_approach: Keep parent and fragment separate. KPV lacks the His-Phe-Arg-Trp core that melanocortin-receptor binding depends on, and reviews describe it as lacking α-MSH's pigmentary action. Findings for the full hormone describe the full hormone.

sections.heading: Findings Depend on the Model
sections.problem: KPV results come from cell lines, chemically induced colitis, T-cell-transfer colitis, peritonitis and skin models. They do not all agree. In one study, KPV reduced neutrophil accumulation in mice but did not suppress macrophage mediator release in vitro.
sections.research_approach: Record the model, species, cell type, chemical form and endpoint for every paper cited. Read agreement and disagreement at that level, rather than summarising the literature as one effect.

sections.heading: Mechanistic Language Is Not a Therapeutic Claim
sections.problem: Phrases such as “reduced inflammation” in a paper describe a measured marker in a defined system. Retold online, they turn into promises about people.
sections.research_approach: Keep the qualifier with the finding: which marker, which model, compared with what. When a statement cannot be traced to a specific experiment, treat it as unsupported.

sections.heading: Building a Reproducible Record
sections.problem: Months later, a result is hard to interpret if nobody recorded which lot, which form and which document the material came with.
sections.research_approach: File the COA against the lot number on the vial. Note the chemical form, counter-ion, storage conditions on receipt, and any in-house identity checks. That record is what lets a result be repeated, or explained when it is not.

L_aeo_direct_answers.a: KPV peptide is the tripeptide Lys-Pro-Val, the C-terminal residues 11–13 of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH). Its reference free-acid form has the formula C₁₆H₃₀N₄O₄, an average molecular weight of 342.44 g/mol, CAS number 67727-97-3 and PubChem CID 125672. It is studied in cell and animal models of inflammatory signaling and is supplied by Veracue for Research Use Only.

KPV is made of three amino acids joined by peptide bonds: lysine, proline and valine, in that order. In the reference compound all three are L-amino acids and the chain ends as a free carboxylic acid. Commercial materials may instead be salts, commonly acetate, or modified forms such as the C-terminal amide, which is why the chemical form should be stated.

In published experiments, KPV entered intestinal and immune cell lines through the PepT1 transporter and reduced NF-κB-linked inflammatory signaling after cytokine stimulation. In mouse models it changed measured inflammatory endpoints. Its mechanism is still debated. These findings describe experimental systems only; they do not describe effects in people.

L_aeo_direct_answers.q: What is KPV peptide studied for?
L_aeo_direct_answers.a: Researchers study KPV for inflammatory signaling in epithelial and immune cells, di- and tripeptide transport through PepT1, the structure–function relationship between α-MSH and its fragments, pharmacology in rodent colitis models, and colon-targeted delivery systems. Analogs such as KdPT and D-residue variants support structure–activity comparisons.

KPV research reports measured activities in models, not established benefits in people. Cell studies showed reduced NF-κB-linked signaling; mouse studies showed lower colitis scores, reduced ear swelling and reduced neutrophil accumulation. No peer-reviewed human efficacy trial was identified, so these findings do not establish any human health outcome.

KPV is characterized mainly by RP-HPLC, which reports chromatographic purity as area percent, and by mass spectrometry, which checks mass against the expected form. Because sequence isomers and D-residue variants share KPV's mass, full confirmation may also need MS/MS fragmentation, reference-standard comparison or chiral analysis.

L_aeo_direct_answers.q: What should a KPV COA contain?
L_aeo_direct_answers.a: A KPV COA should name the exact sequence and chemical form, including any counter-ion, and carry a lot number matching the vial. It should list the testing laboratory and date, an HPLC result with chromatogram, and a mass result stating whether neutral or protonated mass is reported, with tolerance.

As of this page's preparation, Veracue's public COA archive did not include a KPV report, so lot-specific KPV documentation is not publicly specified. Veracue's Certificates page provides a route to request lot documentation through its contact page. Any KPV COA should be matched to the lot number printed on the vial before its results are relied on.

L_aeo_direct_answers.q: What is the difference between KPV and related peptides?
L_aeo_direct_answers.a: KPV (Lys-Pro-Val) is a 3-residue fragment of α-MSH. α-MSH is the 13-residue parent hormone, which acts on melanocortin receptors. KdPT (Lys-D-Pro-Thr) is a related derivative matching IL-1β residues 193–195. GHK-Cu is an unrelated copper tripeptide, and BPC-157 is a 15-residue synthetic peptide.

L_aeo_direct_answers.q: Does Veracue provide KPV dosage instructions?
L_aeo_direct_answers.a: No. Veracue does not provide KPV dosage, dosing schedules, routes or administration guidance, because the material is sold for Research Use Only and no human dose has been established in peer-reviewed clinical research. Laboratory conditions are set by each study's own validated design.

M_faq.a: KPV is a synthetic tripeptide, Lys-Pro-Val, identical to the last three residues of α-MSH. It is studied in laboratory models of inflammatory signaling and is supplied for Research Use Only.

M_faq.q: What is the KPV peptide sequence?
M_faq.a: The sequence is lysine–proline–valine, written Lys-Pro-Val or K-P-V. The reference compound is H-Lys-Pro-Val-OH, with all three residues in the L-configuration.

M_faq.q: What is the molecular weight of KPV?
M_faq.a: The free acid (C₁₆H₃₀N₄O₄) has an average molecular weight of 342.44 g/mol and a monoisotopic mass of 342.2267 Da. Other forms, such as the C-terminal amide or acetate salt, differ, so the form should be confirmed first.

M_faq.q: Is KPV the same as α-MSH?
M_faq.a: No. α-MSH is a 13-residue hormone. KPV is only its final three residues. It lacks the His-Phe-Arg-Trp core linked to melanocortin-receptor binding, and reviews describe it as lacking the hormone's pigmentary action.

M_faq.q: What is KPV studied for in research?
M_faq.a: Mainly inflammatory signaling in cell lines, PepT1-mediated peptide transport, rodent colitis models, α-MSH structure–function questions and colon-targeted delivery systems.
In experiments, it reduced NF-κB-linked signaling in stimulated cell lines and changed inflammatory measures in mouse models. These are model-specific observations, not effects in people.

M_faq.q: What are the benefits of KPV peptide?
M_faq.a: No human benefits have been established. Published findings come from cell and animal models, and each applies only to the model and endpoint in which it was measured.

M_faq.q: Does KPV act through melanocortin receptors?
M_faq.a: The evidence suggests not primarily. One study reported colitis effects at least partly independent of MC1R. Another proposed interference with IL-1β signaling. PepT1 uptake has also been reported. The mechanism remains unresolved.

M_faq.q: What is the recommended KPV dosage or dosing?
M_faq.a: Veracue provides no dosage or dosing information. KPV is a Research Use Only material, no human dose has been established in peer-reviewed clinical research, and experimental conditions belong to each study's own design.

M_faq.q: Does Veracue provide guidance on oral KPV?
M_faq.a: No. Veracue provides no oral-use, formulation or administration guidance. Published gut-targeted studies used experimental carrier systems in animal models and are not instructions for any use.
Usually by mass spectrometry, supported where needed by MS/MS fragmentation for residue order, comparison with a reference standard, and chiral analysis for stereochemistry.

M_faq.q: What does HPLC purity tell you about KPV?
M_faq.a: It reports the main peak's share of total detected peak area at one wavelength. It describes cleanliness, not identity, and should be read alongside the chromatogram.

M_faq.q: Can mass spectrometry alone confirm KPV?
M_faq.a: Not completely. Lys-Val-Pro, Pro-Val-Lys and D-residue variants have the same mass as KPV. Intact mass supports identity but does not prove sequence order or configuration.

M_faq.q: What is the difference between KPV free base and KPV acetate?
M_faq.a: The free base is the peptide alone. The acetate is a salt in which acetate counter-ions accompany the peptide, so a given weight of powder contains less peptide. A COA should name the form.

M_faq.q: What should a KPV Certificate of Analysis include?
M_faq.a: Sequence and chemical form, lot number, testing lab and date, HPLC result with chromatogram, and a mass result with its reporting convention and tolerance.

M_faq.q: Does Veracue publish a KPV COA?

acceptedAnswer.text: KPV is a synthetic tripeptide, Lys-Pro-Val, identical to the last three residues of α-MSH. It is studied in laboratory models of inflammatory signaling and is supplied for Research Use Only.

mainEntity.name: What is the KPV peptide sequence?

acceptedAnswer.text: The sequence is lysine–proline–valine, written Lys-Pro-Val or K-P-V. The reference compound is H-Lys-Pro-Val-OH, with all three residues in the L-configuration.

mainEntity.name: What is the molecular weight of KPV?

acceptedAnswer.text: The free acid (C₁₆H₃₀N₄O₄) has an average molecular weight of 342.44 g/mol and a monoisotopic mass of 342.2267 Da. Other forms, such as the C-terminal amide or acetate salt, differ, so the form should be confirmed first.

mainEntity.name: Is KPV the same as α-MSH?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. α-MSH is a 13-residue hormone. KPV is only its final three residues. It lacks the His-Phe-Arg-Trp core linked to melanocortin-receptor binding, and reviews describe it as lacking the hormone's pigmentary action.

mainEntity.name: What is KPV studied for in research?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mainly inflammatory signaling in cell lines, PepT1-mediated peptide transport, rodent colitis models, α-MSH structure–function questions and colon-targeted delivery systems.
In experiments, it reduced NF-κB-linked signaling in stimulated cell lines and changed inflammatory measures in mouse models. These are model-specific observations, not effects in people.

mainEntity.name: What are the benefits of KPV peptide?

acceptedAnswer.text: No human benefits have been established. Published findings come from cell and animal models, and each applies only to the model and endpoint in which it was measured.

mainEntity.name: Does KPV act through melanocortin receptors?

acceptedAnswer.text: The evidence suggests not primarily. One study reported colitis effects at least partly independent of MC1R. Another proposed interference with IL-1β signaling. PepT1 uptake has also been reported. The mechanism remains unresolved.

mainEntity.name: What is the recommended KPV dosage or dosing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Veracue provides no dosage or dosing information. KPV is a Research Use Only material, no human dose has been established in peer-reviewed clinical research, and experimental conditions belong to each study's own design.

mainEntity.name: Does Veracue provide guidance on oral KPV?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Veracue provides no oral-use, formulation or administration guidance. Published gut-targeted studies used experimental carrier systems in animal models and are not instructions for any use.
Usually by mass spectrometry, supported where needed by MS/MS fragmentation for residue order, comparison with a reference standard, and chiral analysis for stereochemistry.

mainEntity.name: What does HPLC purity tell you about KPV?

acceptedAnswer.text: It reports the main peak's share of total detected peak area at one wavelength. It describes cleanliness, not identity, and should be read alongside the chromatogram.

mainEntity.name: Can mass spectrometry alone confirm KPV?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not completely. Lys-Val-Pro, Pro-Val-Lys and D-residue variants have the same mass as KPV. Intact mass supports identity but does not prove sequence order or configuration.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between KPV free base and KPV acetate?

acceptedAnswer.text: The free base is the peptide alone. The acetate is a salt in which acetate counter-ions accompany the peptide, so a given weight of powder contains less peptide. A COA should name the form.

mainEntity.name: What should a KPV Certificate of Analysis include?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sequence and chemical form, lot number, testing lab and date, HPLC result with chromatogram, and a mass result with its reporting convention and tolerance.

mainEntity.name: Does Veracue publish a KPV COA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not at the time this page was prepared. Lot documentation can be requested through Veracue's contact page, as described on the Certificates page.
